# DRAFT: Certifier statement on disaster relationship

> **Draft prepared by Counted for review. Not a death certificate. Not valid until reviewed and signed by the
> certifying medical examiner, coroner or physician.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Case | 6cbe2c307eb3 |
| Decedent | age 66, male |
| Date of death | 2017-09-14 |
| Location | Collier County, FL |
| Disaster | Hurricane Irma (DR-4337-FL); incident period 2017-09-04 to 2017-10-18 |
| NWS warnings in force | Storm Surge Watch (2017-09-07), Hurricane Watch (2017-09-07), Storm Surge Warning (2017-09-08), Hurricane Warning (2017-09-08), Flood Watch (2017-09-08) |
| Cause on certificate (per family) | carbon monoxide |

## Determination (CDC 2017 Reference Guide)
In my opinion this death was **indirectly caused** by Hurricane Irma (DR-4337-FL).

**Causal chain:** Hurricane Irma caused a five-day power outage; loss of utility power led the decedent to operate a gasoline-powered generator inside a partially enclosed garage, producing lethal carbon monoxide accumulation, resulting in carbon monoxide poisoning death at home.

**Proposed "How injury occurred" (Item 43):** During a five-day power outage caused by Hurricane Irma (DR-4337-FL), decedent operated a gasoline-powered generator inside a residential garage with the door partially closed; accumulated carbon monoxide migrated into the living space and caused fatal poisoning.

**Proposed wording for FEMA Funeral Assistance** (FEMA rejects "may have been caused by"):
> This death was indirectly caused by Hurricane Irma (DR-4337-FL).

## Family account (verbatim)
- "After Hurricane Irma we had no power for five days, so he ran the generator in the garage with the door half closed" (carbon monoxide)

## Panel
| Seat | Determination | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| CDC decision tree | indirect | 0.85 |
| Examiner (Claude) | indirect | 0.97 |
| Examiner (Amazon Nova) | indirect | 0.95 |

Unanimous: yes. Open questions: Autopsy or toxicology report confirming elevated carboxyhemoglobin (COHb) saturation; Medical examiner or coroner official cause-of-death confirmation specifying carbon monoxide poisoning; Utility outage records for the specific address corroborating the five-day power loss.

# Funeral Assistance: what to gather

We are very sorry for your loss. FEMA may help with funeral costs when a death was caused directly or indirectly by a declared disaster.

Good news: FEMA Individual Assistance was approved for Collier County under DR-4337-FL. Funeral Assistance is part of that program.

- [ ] Death certificate, OR the signed certifier statement Counted drafted (ask the medical examiner or doctor to review and sign it)
- [ ] Funeral home contract or itemized receipts
- [ ] Proof of any other help received (insurance, burial societies, donations)
- [ ] The decedent's and applicant's names and addresses

Apply at DisasterAssistance.gov or call 1-800-621-3362. If FEMA says no, you can appeal in writing using the appeal letter below.

## Appeal letter (fill in and sign)

> I am appealing FEMA's decision on Funeral Assistance for __________, who died on 2017-09-14 in Collier County. The enclosed statement from the certifier states the death was indirectly caused by Hurricane Irma (DR-4337-FL): Hurricane Irma caused a five-day power outage; loss of utility power led the decedent to operate a gasoline-powered generator inside a partially enclosed garage, producing lethal carbon monoxide accumulation, resulting in carbon monoxide poisoning death at home.. I ask FEMA to reconsider.

_Counted cannot promise any outcome. FEMA makes the decision._
